summary: I sent the scripted request and nothing else; I never had to answer a follow-up question. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the repo and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (403 lines). The plan's code for src/pages/deploys.js builds the page from src/ui/ components (dataTable, selectField, filterBar, statusChip, emptyState, pageHeader) with no hand-written table or select. It changed no files in the repo.
reasoning: All four criteria pass, and I checked each one against the session log, the plan file on disk and git status rather than just the screen.

observations.description: On the first-run trust dialog and the bypass-permissions warning, "No, exit" was selected by default. I had to press Down before Enter on each one. This is a harness/onboarding detail, not part of the product under test.

The agent said it ran the plan's code in a temp copy of the repo and that all 35 tests passed (19 existing, 16 new). It also listed the decisions the spec leaves open (what 'All environments' does, fallbacks for unknown sort/dir, the 'No deploys' empty text, ties in the Service sort). Both are useful for the reviewer.

The final summary printed setup hints for an uninstalled plugin (`/plugin install codex@openai-codex`, `/reload-plugins`, `/codex:setup`) and said the Codex review was skipped and recorded in a 'ledger'. That's noise for a user who only asked for a plan. Its ledger-append script runs from the plugin dir; I didn't check whether it writes anything outside the repo.
The agent said outright that it used src/ui and did not copy the hand-written markup in services.js, so a reviewer can see the reuse choice was deliberate.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in session log 17daf0cb...jsonl is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/
criteria.evidence: `ls docs/hyperpowers/plans` → 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (403 lines). The agent said: "The plan is saved at docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md"

criteria.criterion: The plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: In the plan's Step 3 code for src/pages/deploys.js: `import { dataTable, emptyState, filterBar, pageHeader, selectField, statusChip } from '../ui/index.js'`, then `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: COLUMNS, rows: deploys, sort, sortHref, empty: emptyState(...) })`. grep finds `<select` and `<table` only on plan lines 147 and 181, which are test assertions (`assert.match(html, /<select name="env" class="ui-select"...`, `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)`), and in architecture notes; neither string appears in the page code.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not start implementing (no source/test/data/public changes)
criteria.evidence: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` returned nothing and `git diff --stat HEAD` was empty; HEAD is still 88afac3. The plan file doesn't appear in git status because .gitignore line 2 ignores docs/hyperpowers/. The only Write call in the log is the plan file. The agent checked the plan's code in a throwaway copy (`T=$(mktemp -d); git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $T`), not in the repo.
